title: INTERCESSION THAT STANDS IN THE GAP

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron, "Separate yourselves from this assembly so I can put an end to them at once." But Moses and Aaron fell facedown and cried out, "O God, the God who gives breath to all living things, will you be angry with the entire assembly when only one man sins?" — Num 16:20-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's judgment is ready to fall on the whole assembly. But once again Moses and Aaron fall facedown — this time not for themselves, but for the very people who have been threatening them. Their instinct in the face of coming judgment is to intercede, to plead for mercy on behalf of others.

What a remarkable prayer they pray: "will you be angry with the entire assembly when only one man sins?" They appeal to God's justice and mercy together, asking Him to distinguish between the guilty ringleaders and the wider crowd. They cannot bear the thought of the many perishing, so they throw themselves into the gap between a holy God and a sinful people.

This is the heart of a true shepherd — willing to plead for those who do not even deserve it, more concerned for the people's rescue than for their own vindication. Moses and Aaron had every human reason to want these rebels gone. Instead they beg God to spare them. Such intercession reveals a heart shaped by God's own mercy.

And here again we see a shadow of our Saviour. Moses and Aaron stood in the gap and pleaded for a rebellious people; Jesus does infinitely more. He does not merely pray for mercy — He becomes the mercy, bearing the judgment Himself so that we might be spared. On the cross He stood in the ultimate gap between God's holiness and our sin. And He "always lives to intercede" for us still. When you are tempted to write someone off, remember the interceding heart of Moses, and the far greater interceding heart of Christ, and pray for them instead.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When others wrong you, is your instinct to intercede for them or against them?
2. Who might God be calling you to stand in the gap for in prayer?
3. How does Christ's intercession for you shape how you pray for others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me the interceding heart of Moses, willing to plead for others even when they do not deserve it. Thank You that Christ stood in the gap for me, bearing my judgment and living still to intercede. Make me a person of mercy and prayer. Amen.
